scope: Pinned-source analysis of the bridge startup continuation. Identifies required observer coverage; does not establish runtime fault detection, stack equivalence or rollback.
findings: The bridge registers start_cb as cbStartOfSimulation with the explicit bridge context as user_data. It is a simulator_callback, not a sync_callback or executing generic-event wrapper.

vpiStartOfSim removes the current callback from StartOfSimulation before invoking it. The callback remains live in the local cur reference and is deleted only after its function returns. Traversing the pending list alone misses the suspended active callback.

After port metadata and outgoing values are initialized, start_cb calls next_advance_cb directly. That direct call yields to SPICE and can repeat its yield without returning while no positive tick advance is scheduled. The registered function remains start_cb; it must not be compared with next_advance_cb.

The startup callback constructor sets only cb_time.type to vpiSuppressTime. Its high, low and real storage is unspecified and must not be serialized. The known bridge registration is static zero-initialized, but this does not authorize reading optional fields of unrelated simulator callbacks.

End-of-compile callbacks and scheduler initialization events execute before vpiStartOfSim. The main scheduler and signals_capture occur after its return. This bounds where startup continuation lives; it does not establish correctness of all initialization events.
The current VF inventory enumerates robotron_sync_live only. Empty generic wrapper or sync inventories at a startup pause therefore cannot establish complete callback coverage.
requiredImplementation: Register simulator-callback lifetimes and record the active pre/post callback independently of pending lists. Cover pending and executing states, cancellation and destruction without dereferencing unknown handles.

Hand off the known startup function/context explicitly. At paused board boundaries validate original lifetime, reason, function, context and internal time pointer/type; do not inspect suppressed time words or unrelated optional payloads.

Exercise restored function, context, time-pointer and list/active-identity faults, including a non-head pending callback. Restore before scheduling or deletion; retain exact callback ordering and continuation controls.

Prove the board startup handoff and later destruction in matched original/disabled/observed runs, then include startup and recovery rejection controls. Keep stack/freed-storage and general rollback claims separate.
